newsitem.title: FRANCE: TIETMEYER SEES GERMAN 97 GROWTH AT TWO PCT OR MORE.
newsitem.headline: TIETMEYER SEES GERMAN 97 GROWTH AT TWO PCT OR MORE.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Wednesday he was confident Germany could achieve economic growth of at least two percent in 1997.
"I think we have a good chance to reach growth of two percent," he told reporters after a France-Germany economic meeting.
"Nobody can be sure," he added, noting that growth could be between two and three percent.
Tietmeyer brushed off questions about the risk that monetary union will not start on time because Germany might not make the grade to take part in the planned launch in January 1999.
"Germany is trying to meet the criteria," he said.
"There is a timetable and the decision will be taken later. There is no reason to talk about this," Tietmeyer said.
